title: Alzheimer's disease · APOE ε2/ε3/ε4
summary: APOE ε4 is the strongest common genetic link to late-onset Alzheimer's disease. ε2 is linked to lower average risk. Two variants, rs429358 and rs7412, work together to define ε2, ε3, and ε4. This report shows them separately, so both are needed. APOE does not predict an outcome. Age, heart health, other genes, and environment also shape risk.

interpretations.TT: In plain words: this means no ε4 allele — together with your rs7412 result below, it determines whether your type is ε2/ε2, ε2/ε3, or ε3/ε3. No copies of the ε4-tagging C allele at rs429358. Combined with rs7412, this typically corresponds to ε2 or ε3 alleles, which are associated with average or lower-than-average Alzheimer's risk. Genetics is only one small factor in overall risk.
interpretations.CT: Plainly, this often means one ε4 allele. Your rs7412 result completes the picture. C/C there means ε3/ε4. A T there almost always means ε2/ε4. One C copy at rs429358 tags ε4. With rs7412 C on the same chromosome, studies link it to about 2 to 4 times the odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease. The effect differs by ancestry. Many carriers never develop the condition.
interpretations.CC: Plainly, this often means ε4/ε4. Two C copies tag two ε4 alleles, and rs7412 is almost always C on those chromosomes. European-ancestry studies link ε4/ε4 to about 8 to 12 times the odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease. Some other ancestry groups have lower estimates. Many carriers never develop dementia. This is a risk link, not a certainty.

In plain words: this means no ε2 allele — together with your rs429358 result above, it determines whether your type is ε3/ε3, ε3/ε4, or ε4/ε4. No copies of the ε2-tagging T allele at rs7412. Your ε2/ε3/ε4 status is then determined by rs429358: C there tags ε4, T there tags ε3. This variant alone does not change your risk estimate.
interpretations.CT: In plain words: this corresponds to one ε2 allele — your rs429358 result above completes the picture: T/T there means ε2/ε3, while a C there almost always means ε2/ε4. One copy of the ε2-tagging T allele, typically indicating one ε2 allele. ε2 is associated on average with somewhat lower odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease relative to the common ε3 allele. This is a modest average effect and only one small factor in overall risk.
interpretations.TT: In plain words: this corresponds to ε2/ε2 (rs429358 is essentially always T on ε2 chromosomes). Two copies of the ε2-tagging T allele, consistent with an ε2/ε2 genotype (roughly 1 in 200 people). ε2/ε2 is associated on average with lower odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease than ε3/ε3. As with all APOE genotypes, this shifts average risk only — it is not protective in any absolute sense.

title: Parkinson's disease · LRRK2 G2019S
summary: LRRK2 G2019S (rs34637584) is the most common known single-gene contributor to Parkinson's disease. It appears in about 1% of cases without a family history and 4% of family-linked cases. It is more common in people with Ashkenazi Jewish or North African ancestry. Most carriers do not develop Parkinson's disease. Later family studies estimate that about 25% to 43% develop it by age 80, with wide ranges between groups.

interpretations.GG: No copies of the G2019S variant. This is the result for the vast majority of people. It says nothing about the many other genetic and non-genetic factors that influence Parkinson's risk.
interpretations.AG: One copy of the G2019S variant (the A allele). Carriers show substantially higher average risk of Parkinson's disease, but penetrance is incomplete — studies estimate roughly 25-45% of carriers develop the condition by age 80, meaning most carriers do not. Because array results can be wrong for rare variants, an unexpected positive result here deserves confirmation and discussion with a genetic counselor before drawing conclusions. This variant is one factor among many.
interpretations.AA: Two copies of the G2019S variant — an extremely rare result. Homozygous carriers appear to have a similar disease course to heterozygous carriers. Penetrance remains incomplete, and an unexpected result of this kind should be confirmed with clinical-quality sequencing and discussed with a genetic counselor.

title: Parkinson's disease · GBA1 N370S
summary: GBA1 N370S (rs76763715, also called N409S) is a strong genetic risk factor for Parkinson's disease. In a large study, carriers of GBA1 variants that included N370S had about five times the average odds. N370S is most common in people with Ashkenazi Jewish ancestry. Most carriers never develop Parkinson's disease. On the Ensembl forward strand, this variant changes T to C.

interpretations.TT: No copies of the N370S variant. This is the most common result and carries no particular association with Parkinson's risk from this variant. Many other factors, genetic and otherwise, contribute to overall risk.
interpretations.CT: One copy of N370S, the C allele on the forward strand. A large study found about five times the odds of Parkinson's disease across GBA1 variant carriers. Some developed it earlier. Lifetime risk for carriers is still estimated below 30%, so most are never affected. Rare array calls can be wrong, so confirm before acting.
interpretations.CC: Two copies of N370S. This result can cause type 1 Gaucher disease, a recessive condition with a wide range of severity. It is also linked to higher Parkinson's risk. Rare array calls need confirmation with clinical testing. A genetic counselor can help explain what it may mean for you and your family.

citations.label: Sidransky et al., N Engl J Med 2009

title: Tauopathy risk · MAPT H1/H2 haplotype
summary: A common chromosome 17 inversion creates two old forms of the MAPT region, called H1 and H2. rs8070723 tags them. H1 is more common and is linked to higher average odds of progressive supranuclear palsy (PSP), a rare tau disease. It also has a smaller link to Parkinson's disease. H2 is linked to lower average odds. Both conditions stay uncommon.

interpretations.AA: Two copies of the H1-tagging A allele (H1/H1), the most common genotype in most populations. H1/H1 is associated with higher average odds of PSP — a rare condition, so the absolute risk stays low — and with modestly higher odds of Parkinson's disease. This haplotype is one small factor among many influences on neurodegenerative risk.
interpretations.AG: One H1 and one H2 haplotype (A/G). Associated with intermediate, near-average risk for the tauopathy-related conditions linked to this region. This common genotype is one small factor among many.
interpretations.GG: Two copies of the H2-tagging G allele (H2/H2), found in roughly 5% of Europeans and rarer elsewhere. H2 is associated with lower average odds of PSP and modestly lower odds of Parkinson's disease. This is a modest average association, not a guarantee of protection.

title: ALS susceptibility · UNC13A
summary: The UNC13A variant rs12608932 is a replicated susceptibility marker for amyotrophic lateral sclerosis (ALS) and frontotemporal dementia, with a small effect on average odds (about 1.1-1.2 fold per C allele). Note: the most important known genetic factor in ALS, the C9orf72 repeat expansion, is a structural variant that genotyping arrays cannot detect — its absence from this report is a limitation of the technology, not evidence you lack it.

interpretations.AA: No copies of the C risk allele. Average odds of ALS at this locus. ALS is rare (lifetime risk around 1 in 300-400), and this common variant is one very small factor among many genetic and environmental influences.
interpretations.AC: One copy of the C allele, associated on average with slightly higher odds of ALS (roughly 1.1-1.2 fold per allele). Because ALS is rare, this barely changes absolute risk. Some studies also link this allele to shorter survival after onset. One very small factor among many.
interpretations.CC: Two C copies, a common genotype linked to slightly higher average odds of ALS. Studies also link it to frontotemporal dementia with TDP-43 changes. The absolute risk stays low. Most people with this genotype are never affected, and it is one small factor among many.

citations.label: van Es et al., Nat Genet 2009

title: Parkinson's disease · SNCA
summary: Common variation near SNCA, the gene for alpha-synuclein, shows the strongest genome-wide association with sporadic Parkinson's disease. The tag SNP rs356182 shifts average odds by about 1.3 fold per G allele. Because Parkinson's affects roughly 1-2% of people over 65, this common variant moves absolute risk only slightly and is one small factor among many.

interpretations.AA: Two copies of the A allele, associated on average with somewhat lower odds of Parkinson's disease at this locus. A modest average effect — one small factor among the many genes and exposures that shape risk.
interpretations.AG: One G and one A allele — an intermediate, near-average result for Parkinson's odds at this locus. This common variant is one small factor among many.
interpretations.GG: Two copies of the G allele, which large genome-wide studies associate with higher average odds of Parkinson's disease (about 1.3 fold per allele). The absolute change in risk is small, and this is one small factor among many genetic and environmental influences; most people with this genotype are never affected.

title: Alzheimer's disease · TREM2 R47H
summary: The rare TREM2 R47H variant (rs75932628, a C-to-T change on the forward strand) is associated with roughly 2-4 fold higher average odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease — an effect size approaching that of one APOE ε4 allele. It is carried by fewer than 1 in 200 people of European ancestry and is rarer in other populations. Most carriers never develop the condition.

interpretations.CC: No copies of the R47H variant — the result for over 99% of people. This says nothing about other Alzheimer's risk factors such as APOE, age, or cardiovascular health.
interpretations.CT: One copy of the R47H variant (the T allele). Two independent 2013 studies associated this variant with roughly 2-4 fold higher average odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease, thought to act through reduced microglial function. Absolute risk still depends far more on age and other factors, and many carriers are never affected — this is one factor among many. Rare-variant array calls can be unreliable, so confirmation is sensible.
interpretations.TT: Two copies of R47H. This result is extremely rare and has been reported only a few times. An array call this rare is likely to be a test error. Confirm it with clinical-quality sequencing before trying to interpret it.

citations.label: Jonsson et al., N Engl J Med 2013
Guerreiro et al., N Engl J Med 2013

title: Alzheimer's disease · CLU
summary: Common variation in the clusterin gene (CLU) was among the first loci beyond APOE to show genome-wide-significant association with late-onset Alzheimer's disease. The minor T allele of rs11136000 is associated with modestly lower average odds (about 0.86 fold per allele). The effect is small: this variant is one small factor among many and shifts absolute risk only slightly.

interpretations.TT: Two copies of T, linked to modestly lower average odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease. Discovery studies found about 0.86 times the odds per T copy. This is a small average effect and one factor among many.
interpretations.CT: One C and one T allele — a common, intermediate result associated with roughly average odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease at this locus. One small factor among many.
interpretations.CC: Two copies of the common C allele. This result is linked to slightly higher average odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease than results with T. The effect is small beside age and APOE. It cannot predict whether one person will be affected.

title: Alzheimer's disease · BIN1
summary: BIN1 is the second-most significant common risk locus for late-onset Alzheimer's disease after APOE in large genome-wide meta-analyses. The T allele of rs6733839 is associated with about 1.2 fold higher average odds per copy. As with all common risk variants, the absolute effect is small and this is one small factor among many.

interpretations.CC: No copies of the T risk allele — associated with average-to-slightly-lower odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease at this locus. One small factor among the many genes and lifestyle influences that shape risk.
interpretations.CT: One copy of the T allele, associated on average with about 1.2 fold higher odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease. This is a small shift compared with the effects of age or APOE ε4, and one small factor among many.
interpretations.TT: Two copies of T, a common genotype found in about 15% of people. It is linked to modestly higher average odds of late-onset Alzheimer's disease. The absolute difference is small, and most people with this result are never affected. It is one factor among many.

title: Frontotemporal dementia · TMEM106B
summary: Common variants near TMEM106B were found in a genome-wide study of frontotemporal lobar degeneration with TDP-43 changes (FTLD-TDP). rs1990622 A is linked to higher average odds, while G is linked to lower odds. The effect seems strongest in people with rare GRN mutations or C9orf72 repeat expansions. FTD is uncommon, so this variant alone changes absolute risk little.

interpretations.AA: Two copies of A, linked to higher average odds of FTLD-TDP. Studies mainly show this as a risk modifier in people with rare GRN mutations or C9orf72 repeat expansions. Without those variants, absolute FTD risk stays low. This common result is one factor among many.
interpretations.AG: One A and one G allele — an intermediate result associated with near-average odds of FTLD-TDP at this locus. One small factor among many influences on neurodegenerative risk.
interpretations.GG: Two copies of the G allele, associated on average with lower odds of FTLD-TDP; in studies of GRN and C9orf72 mutation carriers this genotype tracked with reduced penetrance. A modest protective association on average, not a guarantee — and one small factor among many.
